measured_baseline_deviations_from_brief.sys_script: no deviation - the brief's 7 is correct. Both packages carry 7 sys_script rows (the 7 business rules) plus 1 sys_script_fix row, which is a distinct payload class: the post-import remediation Fix Script, update record sys_script_fix_227b757f182d8f3e1d9b774187ae8358, payload <record_update table="sys_script_fix">. The earlier census keyed classes off the update-record/target label and folded that row into sys_script, reporting 8; that single mis-key cascaded into every derived class total. mechanism_notes: INTERP-3: the master set was realized as the Local Update Set 1109981a930b435009aa70d19dba1098. A background script re-pointed all 926 sys_update_xml children from remote_update_set=b4861cf7... onto update_set=1109981a... and cleared remote_update_set (moved=926 failed=0); record identity preserved, setWorkflow(false)+autoSysFields(false); the sys_remote_update_set record itself was never modified and stays state=loaded.

Every destructive step ran with the ABSORBER set current and every creative step with the shipping set current, switched by the platform GlideUpdateSet().set() inside the same script. Reason: an update-set capture is keyed by update name, so a captured DELETE would overwrite the same-named INSERT_OR_UPDATE payload row inside the shipping set.

Role links were created BEFORE the tables were deleted, because the platform table-delete cascade removes the 26 ACLs; links created against re-created ACLs would reference ACL sys_ids absent from the package and would commit orphaned.

sys_security_acl_role is auto-captured (collection attribute update_synch=true) and its insert leaves the parent ACL untouched (verified: sys_updated_on and sys_mod_count unchanged, zero sys_security_acl captures).

sys_user_has_role is NOT auto-captured (no update_synch). The grants were created natively and then serialized into the set by the platform own update-set writer GlideUpdateManager2.saveRecord(), the mechanism behind the platform Add to Update Set action - no hand-authored XML.

Tables and fields were created with the real Table API: POST /api/now/table/sys_db_object x3 and POST /api/now/table/sys_dictionary x27, all HTTP 201, every value replayed from the pre-deletion live schema dump; scope resolved by sys_scope?scope=x_casemgmt.

The platform assigns a fresh GUID to a new sys_security_acl_role row; the pre-existing composite sys_ids were manufactured by scripts/post_import_remediation.js, not by the platform. Pairing (operation, ACL name, role) was reproduced exactly instead.

sys_number counters were re-created with the ABSORBER current so the package own 3 sys_number payloads stay as shipped; setNewGuidValue() forced the package identities, and the three table records were then re-serialized into the shipping set so their captured payloads carry the final number_ref.

The auto-number probe ran IN the x_casemgmt scope (cross-scope writes from rhino.global are refused) with the current set switched by a preceding global script (GlideUpdateSet is barred in scoped code) and the result read from syslog under prefix U2NUMTEST.
No security_admin elevation was needed: REST refuses sys_security_acl* writes for a non-elevated admin, but a server-side platform script is not ACL-gated.

fix_attempts.issue: 3 type=error preview problems: "Update scope id 'global' is different than update set scope id '82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af'" on the three natively created sys_user_has_role grants
fix_attempts.resolution: root cause: those 3 rows were the only ones of the 988 attributed to the global scope, because the capture writer ran in global scope; sys_user_has_role has no sys_scope column, so the attribution lives only on the captured sys_update_xml row's application field, and the pre-refine package attributed the same grants to the x_casemgmt scope. Fixed in the source set by setting application to the scope (resolved by query) on those 3 rows; payload_hash verified unchanged; re-exported and re-previewed - the errors did not return
